text:
maya: Hey team, getting reports that the Console chart for per-region RPS is blank when filtering region=eu + model=v2.1. Customers still see requests (billing spikes) though. Example: https://console.redwood.ai/org/xyz/metrics?model=v2.1&region=eu :confused:
ciara: can you paste repro steps and a screenshot? is this org-level filter or workspace? any customer IDs? :eyes:
maya: repro steps:
1) open console -> analytics -> model metrics
2) set model = v2.1, region = eu, timeframe = last 24h
3) chart area shows "No data" but invoices and usage show calls for that model in EU
Customer ticket: #4532, org: acme-inc. attaching a short video in the ticket.
devon: quick q — is the chart pulling from events-service or from aggregated-timeseries? those are two different query paths.
ciara: looks like the chart should use aggregated-timeseries endpoint. maya, can you try the raw endpoint?
maya: ran the raw endpoint -> `GET /internal/analytics/aggregates?model=v2.1&region=eu&start=...&end=...` returned empty array. But `GET /internal/analytics/events?model_version=v2.1&region=eu` returns matching events.
liam: that smells like a mapping problem between events -> aggregates job. We shipped a mapping rename last night (model_version -> model_ver) in the aggregator. If the frontend still sends model=v2.1 it may not map.
devon: hang on. frontend calls aggregated-timeseries with param `model` not `model_version`. The aggregator expects `model_version`. The rename change in transforms would drop the filter, causing an unfiltered aggregate (or empty) depending on path.
maya: here's the exact curl I used:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" "https://api.redwood.ai/internal/analytics/aggregates?model=v2.1&region=eu&start=1672531200&end=1672617600"
```
returns `[]`
liam: i'm looking at the deploy diff. We changed mapping key in `transforms/ingest_mapping.yml` to `model_ver` to align with an upstream schema. Aggregator's filter code expects `model_version`. So three different names are floating: `model`, `model_version`, `model_ver`. Not great.
analytics-bot: processed backlog: 1,242 events in 00:03:12 (info)
alerts-bot: high-latency detect on aggregates-worker (p95 > 5s) in prod :warning:
devon: possible causes: 1) aggregator dropped filter -> returns global aggregates (looks like frontend treats empty as no data for region), or 2) aggregator timed out and returned empty set. Need logs.
liam: quick mitigation: patch aggregator to accept `model` query param as alias for `model_version` and add tests. I'll open a PR and cut a canary.
ciara: meanwhile we should tell the customer we have a suspected root cause and a patch in progress. also confirm no billing overcharges (ticket #4532 flagged billing spike) — that spike looks real, events exist so billing is correct, just the chart is wrong.
maya: attaching a screenshot of the empty chart + example event from events endpoint (timestamp + request_id) in the ticket.
liam: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/analytics/pull/987 — patch accepts aliases and adds logging when unknown filter keys present. rolling a canary to prod cluster `analytics-canary`.
devon: commands to check logs if you need to triage:
```
kubectl -n prod logs deployment/aggregates-worker --since=2h | grep "filter" | head -n 200
# or check specific request id
kubectl -n prod logs deployment/aggregates-worker | grep 9f2a7b1c
```
liam: canary looks good on eu-az1 for 10m, returning aggregates now. Patching to main and will redeploy. :white_check_mark:
analytics-bot: aggregates-worker canary processed 3k events, p95 restored to 210ms
ciara: thanks — i'll update the customer: explain bug, ETA for full rollout ~20 minutes, tell them analytics data is intact (billing unaffected).
maya: customer updated, they say relieved. i'll monitor ticket in case of follow-ups.
liam: follow-up action items: 1) add compat layer + unit tests (done in PR), 2) add e2e to ensure frontend param names map to aggregator keys, 3) run a job to re-aggregate last 24h for any orgs where aggregates were missed (script in PR).
devon: note for postmortem: inconsistent param naming across services caused a user-facing dashboard bug and confusion. also add runbook step to check aggregator mappings after deploys.
ciara: closing loop with customer. Marking internal incident as Sev-3 (no data in chart, billing unaffected). :thumbsup:
maya: thanks everyone :raised_hands:
